title: Change of rings for the derived tensor
statement:
Let $n,m\in\mathbf Z$, let $\ell$ be a prime with $n=\ell m$, and put $R=\Lambda'=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ and $k=\mathbf F_\ell=\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$. Let $M$ be a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and let $N^\bullet$ be an arbitrary, possibly unbounded, cochain complex of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] such that $\ell N^q=0$ for every $q$. Regard $N^\bullet$ and $M/\ell M$ as $k$-modules via the quotient $R\to k$. Put $M$ and $M/\ell M$ in degree zero. Use the ordinary-module derived tensor computed on K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex, lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], and the derived categories of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
M[0]\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N^\bullet\ \cong\ \operatorname{Res}_{R\to k}\bigl((M/\ell M)[0]\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}N^\bullet\bigr)
$$
in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$, where $\operatorname{Res}_{R\to k}$ means forgetting to $R$-modules along $R\to k$. On ordinary tensor representatives its map is $x\otimes y\mapsto\bar x\otimes y$. Here ordinary module tensor products have their usual universal property for balanced biadditive maps; their total complexes are as in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] on the one-point ringed site.

proof.text:
The map $R\to k$, $[a]_n\mapsto[a]_\ell$, is well-defined because $\ell\mid n$, and its kernel is $\ell R$. Since $\ell N^q=0$, scalar multiplication by a residue class in $k$ is defined by any lift in $R$; two lifts differ by a multiple of $\ell$, which acts by zero. The same applies to $\overline M=M/\ell M$. More generally, for every $k$-module $V$ define
$$\phi_V:M\otimes_R V\longrightarrow\overline M\otimes_k V,\qquad x\otimes v\longmapsto\bar x\otimes v.$$
The displayed rule is $R$-balanced. Its inverse is $\bar x\otimes v\mapsto x\otimes v$: replacing $x$ by $x+\ell z$ changes the tensor by $\ell z\otimes v=z\otimes\ell v=0$; for $c\in k$ choose a lift $a\in R$, and the balancing relation is $ax\otimes v=x\otimes av$. Thus the inverse is $k$-balanced and independent of all lifts. The two composites fix every pure tensor, so these are inverse $R$-linear maps. For any $k$-linear $f:V\to W$ both naturality composites send $x\otimes v$ to $\bar x\otimes f(v)$, so $\phi_V$ is natural in $V$.

proof.text: The module $\overline M$ is flat over $k$. Indeed let $i:V\hookrightarrow W$ be an injective map of $k$-modules. It is still injective as a map of $R$-modules. Flatness of $M$ implies that $M\otimes_R i$ is injective (use the left-tensor assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] on $0\to V\to W$). The natural isomorphisms $\phi_V,\phi_W$ of Step 1 identify this map with $\overline M\otimes_k i$, which is therefore injective. This is precisely the definition of flatness in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No assertion that $k$ itself is flat over $R$ is made or needed.

proof.text: Both $M[0]$ over $R$ and $\overline M[0]$ over $k$ are bounded-above complexes of flat modules: the only nonzero term is in degree zero, and the zero terms are flat since tensoring with zero is zero. Apply [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] to each. They are K-flat even though $N^\bullet$ may be unbounded. Apply clause (2) of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] first with the identity $R\to R$, then with the identity $k\to k$, using the identity K-flat resolutions of these two single-term complexes. It gives canonical representatives $Q_R(M\otimes_R N^\bullet)$ and $Q_k(\overline M\otimes_k N^\bullet)$ of the two derived tensors. The total tensor formula of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] has only the summand $(0,q)$ in degree $q$; its differential is $1\otimes d_N^q$, with sign $(-1)^0=1$.

source.place: Tag 064K (bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat); Tag 06Y6, construction of the mixed derived tensor computed by K-flat complexes

proof.text:
Apply Step 1 to $V=N^q$ in every degree. Naturality for $d_N^q$ says explicitly
$$\phi_{N^{q+1}}(x\otimes d_N^q y)=\bar x\otimes d_N^q y=(1\otimes d_N^q)\phi_{N^q}(x\otimes y).$$
Thus the $\phi_{N^q}$ and their inverses form inverse $R$-linear chain maps $M\otimes_R N^\bullet\cong\operatorname{Res}_{R\to k}(\overline M\otimes_k N^\bullet)$. Restriction of scalars leaves underlying abelian groups, kernels and images unchanged, so preserves cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms. The localization property in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] therefore induces restriction $D(k)\to D(R)$, sending $Q_k(C)$ to $Q_R(\operatorname{Res}C)$. Localize this chain isomorphism and compose with the two canonical representative isomorphisms of Step 3. This proves the asserted isomorphism in $D(R)$. The maps use only the quotient $M\to\overline M$ and tensor universal properties, with no choices of lifts remaining; clause (2) of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] makes the model comparisons canonical independently of resolutions. Hence the resulting derived isomorphism is canonical.
